name: SlopAds
iocPatterns: Malicious Android application distribution via Google Play Store
keyCapabilities: Mobile ad fraud via malicious Android applications
Deployment of backdoored apps through the Google Play Store
Billion‑scale fraudulent ad impression and click generation using hidden WebViews and steganography
Multi‑domain C2 infrastructure with over 300 related domains
Infrastructure acquisition and rental (physical/cloud servers, domains)
Compromise of third‑party web service accounts (GitHub, Twitter, Google, Dropbox, SendGrid)
Creation of local and domain accounts for persistence
Formation of botnets from compromised machines
Targeting Exchange, Office 365, and Google Workspace via credentials or tokens
Automated keyword search in mail with tools such as MailSniper
Endpoint and network denial‑of‑service attacks on email, DNS, and web applications
Legitimate account creation on cloud providers for persistence
Persona development via public social media data
Exploitation of software vulnerabilities to crash services or gain persistence
Hijacking binaries executed by Windows services through improper file permissions
Implantation of malicious code in cloud/container images
recommendedActions: Verify and remove any suspicious or unauthorized mobile advertising applications from user devices and network inventories.
Implement multi‑factor authentication (MFA) on all user, cloud, and service accounts to mitigate hijacking risk.
Monitor audit logs for unauthorized creation of local/domain accounts and flag anomalous account activity.

Detect UAC bypass attempts through endpoint monitoring solutions. Secure third‑party web‑service credentials, implement anomaly detection on sign‑in events, and enforce least privilege. Employ network segmentation and strict access controls to limit the lateral movement of compromised infrastructure. Apply rate limits or DDoS protection services to monitor and mitigate DoS attacks against email, DNS, and web applications. Enforce strict file‑permission settings for Windows service binaries to prevent hijacks. Continuously scan cloud images and container registries for malicious payloads. Use advanced endpoint detection to identify polymorphic code patterns. Audit and restrict privileges that can overwrite critical system binaries or services.
campaignsText: SlopAds demonstrates an ongoing, high‑volume campaign that launched at least 224 malicious Android apps in late 2025, with a global distribution exceeding 38 million downloads. The actor applies a layered approach to operations: initial compromise via the app store, persistence through newly created local/domain accounts and compromised cloud services, and exfiltration or service disruption via distributed DoS attacks. Operational tempo has been aggressive, consistently adding new domains and C2 servers while employing rapidly mutating code to outpace defensive detection. Notable past operations involve orchestrated click‑fraud against major ad exchanges and coordinated denial‑of‑service incidents aimed at disrupting enterprise mail hosts.
description: SlopAds is an advanced mobile ad‑fraud operator that releases nearly 200 malicious Android apps via the Google Play Store to generate billions of fake ad impressions and clicks each day. The group employs a broad attack surface, abusing legitimate cloud services, hijacking binaries, and executing denial‑of‑service or credential‑stealing attacks against enterprise email and collaboration platforms to sustain its operations.
goals: SlopAds’ strategic objective is financial gain through ad‑fraud, complemented by the acquisition of persistent access to high‑value enterprise services. The actor primarily targets sectors where advertising revenue or privileged data is critical—media, finance, defense, and healthcare—and focuses on global markets such as the United States, India, and Brazil. Their targeting profile emphasizes platforms that provide large user bases (Google Play, Office 365, Google Workspace) and infrastructure services that can support massive traffic spikes while remaining difficult to detect.
